```plato
    //==
    // # Sparse system operations
    //
    // The two things a conjugate gradient asks of the assembled matrix: multiply
    // by a vector, and report the diagonal. Both are a single sweep of the
    // coordinate list, and neither reads an element by position.
    //
    // These are the only places in this library that use an affine `Buffer`.
    // Scattering into indexed slots is what a builder is for, and the buffer
    // never escapes the function that allocates it.

    // A number buffer of `n` slots, every one written to `value`. `new
    // Buffer<T>(n)` leaves slot contents to the runtime, so every accumulator
    // below starts here rather than from a bare allocation.
    FilledNumbers(n: Integer, value: Number): Buffer<Number>
    {
        var slots = new Buffer<Number>(n);
        var i = 0;
        while (i < n)
        {
            slots = slots.Set(i, value);
            i = i + 1;
        }
        return slots;
    }
```
